0.1 This Indian Standard (Part 14/Set 1 to 3 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Ind'an Standards on 7 March 1988, after the dra k finalized by the Environmental Testing Procedures Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. 0.2 This standard ( Part 14 ) was originally published in 1978, This revision has been undertaken to align it with the latest international standards. The major deviations in this revision are: a) Test Na The transition time is now prescribed more precisely, and a greater number of exposure times are given.

4 b)

Values of high and low conditioning temperature between which the change is to be effected, The conditioning times for which the test item is kept at these temperatures, The rate of change between these temperatures, The and number of cycles of conditioning,

b) Test

test is prescribed with a Nb -The specified rate of change of temperature and a greater number of exposure times are given. test is no longer restricted NC -The to the use of water and the duration parameters are more strictly described.

Guidance on the choice of suitable test parameters for inclusion in the detail specification is given in IS : 9001 ( Part 3 )-1978*, which should be read in conjunction with this standard. 0.4 This standard is largely based on IEC Pub 68-2-14 ( 1984) `Basic environmental testing procedures: Part 2 Tests -Test N : Change of temperature', issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission ( IEC ). 0.5 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960t.
*Guidance for environmental testing: of temperature. tRuler for rounding off numericaf values

c) Test

0.3 A change of temperature test is intended to determine the effect on the test item of a change of temperature or a succession of changes of temperature. It is not intended to show effects which are due only to the high or low temperature. For these effects, the dry heat test or the cold test should be used.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard (Part 14/Set 1) deals with rapid change of temperature ( thermal shock ) test with prescribed time of transition by two chamber method.
2. TEBMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose

5.1.2 The chambers shall be capable of maintaining the appropriate temperatures, for the test in any region where the item is placed.
5.1.3 The absolute humidity shall not exceed 20 g of water vapour per cubic metre of air (corresponding approximately to 50 percent relative humidity at 35'C ). When testing is performed at a temperature lower than 35"C, relative humidity shall not exceed the 50 percent. 5.1.4 The temperature of walls of dry heat and cold chambers shall not differ by more than 3 percent and 8 percent respectively, from the specified temperature of test, expressed in kelvins. This requirement applies to all parts of the chamber walls and the items shall be unable to `see' any heating or cooling elements which do not comply with this requirement. 5.1.5 The volume of the chambers and the air velocity shall be such that after insertion of the test items, the temperature of the atmosphere shall be within the specified tolerance after a time of not more than 10 percent of the exposure time.

OBJECT

3.1 The object of this test is to determine the ability of components, equipment or other articles to withstand rapid changes of ambient temperature. The exposure times adequate to accomplish this will depend upon the nature of the item.

PART Section 2 14 TEST N : CHANGE OF TEMPERATURE with Test Nb : Change of Temperature ( Temperature Cycling) Specified Rate of Change - One Chamber Method (

First Revision )

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 14/Set 2 ) deals with change of temperature ( temperature cycling) test with specified rate of change by one chamber method.
2. TERMlNOLOGY

4

the change-over from low temperature to high temperature or vice versa may be performed at the rate of change of temperature required for the test.

2.1 For

the purpose of this test, the definitions and e;xplanation of terms given in IS : 9000 (Part 1 )-1977* shall apply.

5.1.2 The absolute humidity shall not exceed 20 g of water vapour per cubic metre of air ( corresponding approximately to 50 percent relative humidity at 35�C). When testing is performed at a temperature lower than 35"C, the relative humidity shall not exceed 50 percent. 5.1.3 During the steady-state temperature periods, the temperature of the walls of the chamber shall not differ within the periods of the high and low temperature by more than 3 percent and 8 percent respectively, of the specified ambient temperature of the test, expressed in kelvins. This requirement applies to all parts of the chambers walls and the items shall be unable to `see' any heating or cooling elements which do not comply with this requirement. 5.1.4 The air of the chamber shall be circulated. Air velocity measured close to the test item shall be not less than 2 m/s. or Supporting of the Test otherwise specified in the relevant specification, the thermal conductivity of the mounting or support shall be low such that for practical purposes the item is thermally When testing several items simulisolated. taneously, they shall be so placed that free air circulation should be provided between items, and between items and chamber surfacf:s.

3. OBJECT

3.1 The
ability articles changes

object of this test is to determine the of components, equipment or other to withstand and/or function during of ambient temperature.

4. GENERAL

DESCRIPTION

OF THE TEST

4.1 The item is exposed to changes of temperature in air by exposure in a chamber to prescribed temperatures varied at a controlled rate. During this exposure the performance of the item may be monitored.

2.1 For

3. OBJECT

3.1 The object of the test is to determine the ability of components, equipment or other changes of rapid withstand articles to temperature.
This test procedure results in a severe thermal shock and is applicable to glass-metal seals and similar items. 4. GENERAL
